checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the ENR eth2 field correctly computed for BPO forks to prevent peer discovery fragmentation?

reachability.notes: If BPO forks incorrectly change next_fork_version, peer discovery would filter out compatible peers, causing network fragmentation at BPO fork boundaries.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the ENR eth2 field computation logic for fork transitions. 2. Locate the code path that handles BPO (Blob Parameter Only) forks vs regular forks. 3. Verify that for BPO forks: next_fork_version == current_fork_version (not changed). 4. Verify that for BPO forks: next_fork_epoch == planned_bpo_epoch. 5. Contrast with regular forks where next_fork_version != current_fork_version. 6. Simulate two clients at a BPO fork boundary and verify they can discover each other via ENR. 7. Test peer filtering logic to ensure BPO fork peers are not incorrectly filtered out. 8. Check for edge cases around epoch boundaries where BPO fork transitions occur.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0051, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Invariant: p2p:SG-012:INV-002. BPO forks are distinct from regular forks in their ENR handling. Incorrect implementation causes network fragmentation by making compatible peers appear incompatible during peer discovery.

checklist.title: Verify P2P Peer Node correctly validates incoming ENR eth2 fields for BPO fork compatibility

reachability.notes: Supporting check for BPO fork ENR validation on the receiving side.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the ENR validation logic in the beacon node when receiving peer ENRs. 2. Verify that the validation correctly interprets BPO fork semantics (next_fork_version == current_fork_version). 3. Test that a peer advertising BPO fork ENR is accepted by compatible nodes. 4. Test that overly strict validation does not reject valid BPO fork ENRs. 5. Verify the peer filtering logic accounts for BPO fork special cases.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0051, Supporting node: actor-beacon-node. This checks the receiving side of ENR validation for BPO fork handling.

checklist.title: Verify P2P Peer actor cannot exploit BPO fork ENR differences to cause network partitioning

reachability.notes: Supporting check for malicious peer exploitation of BPO fork ENR handling.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Assess whether a malicious peer can craft ENR records that exploit differences in BPO fork handling between client implementations. 2. Test if advertising incorrect next_fork_version for BPO forks can cause victim nodes to drop connections. 3. Verify that ENR signing prevents tampering with fork-related fields. 4. Check for timing attacks around BPO fork epoch boundaries. 5. Test interoperability between different client implementations at BPO fork transitions.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0051, Supporting node: actor-p2p-peer. Assesses attack vectors from malicious P2P peers exploiting BPO fork ENR semantics.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is ENR eth2 field correctly set to signal no upcoming fork (next_fork_version == current_fork_version AND next_fork_epoch == FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH)?

reachability.notes: Incorrect no-fork signaling could cause peers to interpret the node as being on a different fork schedule, leading to peer isolation.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the code path where ENR eth2 field is computed (p2p:SG-012:enr_eth2_field_computation). 2. Verify that when no fork is scheduled, next_fork_version is set exactly equal to current_fork_version. 3. Verify that when no fork is scheduled, next_fork_epoch is set to FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH constant. 4. Test edge cases: (a) immediately after a fork completes, (b) when fork schedule is cleared, (c) during node initialization with no planned forks. 5. Capture ENR advertisement and verify peers can correctly parse the no-fork signal. 6. Attempt to trigger peer isolation by misconfiguring fork signaling values.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0052, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Invariant: p2p:SG-012:INV-003. Incorrect FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH handling could cause peer discovery failure and network isolation.

checklist.title: Verify Beacon Node correctly computes no-fork signaling values for P2P peer discovery

reachability.notes: Incorrect no-fork signaling could cause peers to interpret the node as being on a different fork schedule, leading to peer isolation.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review beacon node (actor-beacon-node) implementation for ENR eth2 field generation. 2. Trace the logic that determines whether a fork is planned or not. 3. Verify the FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH constant is correctly defined and used. 4. Check that current_fork_version is accurately retrieved from chain state. 5. Verify no race conditions exist between fork schedule updates and ENR field computation. 6. Test that ENR updates are propagated correctly when fork status changes.
checklist.notes: Supporting check for PROP-0052. Covers actor-beacon-node behavior in computing ENR eth2 fields.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does ENR eth2 field epoch determination use wall-clock time instead of sync state?

reachability.notes: A syncing node using sync-state epoch would advertise a pre-fork fork_digest after the fork has occurred, causing it to be filtered out by fully-synced peers. This creates a bootstrapping problem where syncing nodes cannot find peers.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the code responsible for computing the ENR eth2 field fork digest (p2p:SG-012:enr_eth2_field_computation). 2. Verify that epoch calculation uses system wall-clock time (e.g., time.Now() or equivalent) rather than the node's synced head slot/epoch. 3. Simulate a syncing node scenario where the synced epoch is significantly behind the current wall-clock epoch (e.g., synced to pre-fork epoch while wall-clock is post-fork). 4. Verify the advertised fork_digest in the ENR matches what would be expected for the current wall-clock epoch, not the synced epoch. 5. Test across fork boundaries: ensure a syncing node crossing a fork transition advertises the post-fork fork_digest based on wall-clock time. 6. Verify peer discovery is not impacted when the node is syncing through a fork boundary. 7. Test edge case: node starts syncing during a fork transition period.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0053, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Invariant: p2p:SG-012:INV-004. A syncing node advertising incorrect fork digest based on sync state would be permanently isolated from fully-synced peers, creating an unrecoverable bootstrapping failure.

checklist.title: Verify Beacon Node ENR computation retrieves epoch from wall-clock, not chain head

reachability.notes: Supporting check to verify the implementation detail of epoch source in ENR computation.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review beacon node (actor-beacon-node) code for ENR eth2 field generation. 2. Trace the epoch variable used in fork_digest calculation. 3. Verify epoch is derived from: current_time - genesis_time, NOT from chain head slot. 4. Check for any code paths that might accidentally use head_slot / SLOTS_PER_EPOCH instead of wall-clock epoch. 5. Verify the genesis_time is correctly initialized and consistent. 6. Test with a mock time source to verify wall-clock is correctly used in epoch calculation.
checklist.notes: Supporting check for PROP-0053. Verifies the beacon node correctly sources epoch from wall-clock for ENR computation.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is BlobSidecarsByRoot deprecated protocol fully disabled after FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS?

reachability.notes: Similar to PROP-0047 but for the by-root variant. Consistent deprecation behavior across both variants is critical.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the BlobSidecarsByRoot request handler in the P2P request-response layer. 2. Locate the epoch-based deprecation check logic. 3. Verify that when current_epoch >= FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, ALL BlobSidecarsByRoot requests are rejected with appropriate error response (e.g., RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE or similar). 4. Test at the exact boundary epoch (FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS) to verify the deprecation activates correctly. 5. Verify no partial responses are sent post-deprecation. 6. Confirm consistent behavior with BlobSidecarsByRange deprecation (cross-reference PROP-0047). 7. Test that malicious peers cannot cause resource exhaustion by flooding deprecated protocol requests post-deadline.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0054, Trust Boundary: tb-006, Invariant: p2p:SG-013:INV-001. Post-transition requests represent minor resource waste. The primary concern is ensuring consistent deprecation between BlobSidecarsByRoot and BlobSidecarsByRange variants.

checklist.title: Verify BlobSidecarsByRoot only serves pre-Fulu blobs during transition period

reachability.notes: Similar to PROP-0047 but for the by-root variant. Consistent deprecation behavior across both variants is critical.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify how blob roots are resolved to their originating slot/epoch in the by-root handler. 2. During the transition period (FULU_FORK_EPOCH <= current_epoch < FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS), verify: (a) Requests for pre-Fulu blob roots are served correctly. (b) Requests for post-Fulu blob roots are rejected. 3. Test with valid pre-Fulu blob roots and confirm successful response. 4. Test with valid post-Fulu blob roots and confirm rejection with appropriate error. 5. Test with invalid/unknown roots and verify appropriate error handling (should not leak information about root validity). 6. Verify the root-to-epoch mapping is secure and cannot be manipulated by attacker. 7. Check for timing attacks where epoch classification could change mid-request processing.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0054, Trust Boundary: tb-006. During transition, the deprecated protocol must correctly distinguish pre-Fulu blobs (servable) from post-Fulu blobs (not servable via this protocol).

checklist.title: Verify consistent deprecation behavior between BlobSidecarsByRoot and BlobSidecarsByRange

reachability.notes: Similar to PROP-0047 but for the by-root variant. Consistent deprecation behavior across both variants is critical.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Compare the deprecation logic implementation between BlobSidecarsByRoot and BlobSidecarsByRange handlers. 2. Verify both use the same epoch threshold: FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS. 3. Verify both return consistent error responses for deprecated requests. 4. Verify both have identical transition period behavior (serving only pre-Fulu data). 5. Test scenarios where one variant is deprecated but the other is not, ensuring no inconsistency window exists. 6. Verify client implementations handle both variants' deprecation consistently. 7. Check for any code duplication or shared utility functions that ensure consistent behavior.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0054. Cross-reference with PROP-0047. Inconsistent deprecation between the two variants could confuse implementations and lead to undefined behavior or interoperability issues.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is max_blobs_per_block consistently computed across all client implementations for epoch boundary transitions?

reachability.notes: Cross-client inconsistency in epoch-dependent blob parameters is the primary consensus split vector for EIP-7892. An attacker can craft blocks at parameter-change epochs to exploit any divergence.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all client implementations of get_blob_parameters(epoch) function. 2. For each client, extract the exact formula/logic used to compute max_blobs_per_block for a given epoch. 3. Identify all epoch boundary transition points where max_blobs_per_block changes (e.g., fork activation epochs, parameter update epochs). 4. For each identified transition epoch E: (a) Compute max_blobs_per_block(E) and max_blobs_per_block(E-1) across all clients, (b) Verify all clients return identical values. 5. Test edge cases: first slot of activation epoch, last slot before activation, epoch 0, maximum epoch value. 6. Craft a block at a parameter-change epoch with exactly max_blobs (as computed by one client) and verify all clients reach the same accept/reject decision. 7. If divergence found, document which clients disagree and the consensus split scenario.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0055, Trust Boundary: tb-001, tb-002, Primary Element: p2p:SG-007:beacon_block_kzg_validation, Invariant type: cross-client consistency. PoC requirement: identify an epoch where two clients compute different max_blobs_per_block values and demonstrate the resulting consensus split.

checklist.title: Verify Beacon Node Actor: Does beacon_block_kzg_validation correctly enforce epoch-dependent blob limits from get_blob_parameters?

reachability.notes: Cross-client inconsistency in epoch-dependent blob parameters is the primary consensus split vector for EIP-7892. An attacker can craft blocks at parameter-change epochs to exploit any divergence.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the beacon_block_kzg_validation logic in each client implementation. 2. Trace how max_blobs_per_block from get_blob_parameters(epoch) flows into KZG validation. 3. Verify the epoch used for parameter lookup matches the block's epoch (not current epoch or slot-derived epoch). 4. Test: Submit a block at epoch E with blobs count equal to max_blobs_per_block(E) and verify acceptance. 5. Test: Submit a block at epoch E with blobs count equal to max_blobs_per_block(E)+1 and verify rejection. 6. Test boundary: At epoch transition slot, verify the correct epoch's parameters are used for validation. 7. Verify gossip validation and block processing use identical parameter lookup logic.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0055, Covered Node: actor-beacon-node. This check verifies the internal logic that enforces the cross-client invariant at the validation layer.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the EIP-7917 proposer lookahead deterministic across all client implementations?

reachability.notes: An attacker publishes a sidecar with a proposer_index that is correct according to one client's shuffling but incorrect according to another's. This exploits cross-client proposer assignment divergence.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Set up test environment with at least two different beacon client implementations (e.g., Prysm, Lighthouse, Teku, Nimbus, Lodestar). 2. Synchronize all clients to the same beacon state S at a given slot. 3. For each slot in the proposer lookahead window (typically 32 slots ahead), call compute_proposer_for_slot(S, slot) on each client. 4. Compare the returned proposer_index values across all client implementations. 5. If any divergence is found, document the slot number, the beacon state root, and the differing proposer indices. 6. Test edge cases: epoch boundaries, validator set changes, and states immediately after finalization. 7. Verify that the shuffling algorithm and random seed derivation are identical across implementations. 8. Attempt to craft a sidecar with a proposer_index that is valid on one client but invalid on another to trigger consensus divergence.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0056, Trust Boundaries: tb-010, tb-011, Primary Element: fork:SG-002:upgrade_to_fulu. This is a critical consensus-level vulnerability. Cross-client proposer assignment divergence means some nodes accept blocks/sidecars from proposers that other nodes reject, causing a consensus split at the first divergent slot. The attack vector involves publishing content via P2P gossip that exploits implementation differences in proposer computation.

checklist.title: Verify Beacon Node Proposer Computation: Does the beacon node correctly implement EIP-7917 proposer shuffling?

reachability.notes: An attacker publishes a sidecar with a proposer_index that is correct according to one client's shuffling but incorrect according to another's. This exploits cross-client proposer assignment divergence.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the beacon node implementation of get_beacon_proposer_index() function. 2. Verify the RANDAO reveal mixing is computed identically to the specification. 3. Check that the epoch seed computation follows the exact formula. 4. Verify the compute_shuffled_index() function matches the specification's swap-or-not shuffle. 5. Ensure effective_balance filtering for proposer eligibility is correct. 6. Test with known test vectors from the Ethereum consensus-spec-tests repository. 7. Verify handling of edge cases: empty validator sets, all validators slashed, minimum/maximum effective balances.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0056, Supporting check for actor-beacon-node. Correct implementation of proposer computation in the beacon node is essential for consensus.

checklist.title: Verify Validator Set Consistency: Is the validator set state identical across clients before proposer computation?

reachability.notes: An attacker publishes a sidecar with a proposer_index that is correct according to one client's shuffling but incorrect according to another's. This exploits cross-client proposer assignment divergence.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Compare validator registry state across multiple client implementations at the same slot. 2. Verify effective_balance calculations are identical. 3. Check activation_epoch and exit_epoch processing is consistent. 4. Verify slashing status propagation is deterministic. 5. Test validator state transitions at epoch boundaries. 6. Ensure validator index assignment is deterministic for new deposits.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0056, Supporting check for actor-validator-set. Validator set divergence would cause downstream proposer computation divergence.

checklist.title: Verify Proposer Validation at Gossip Layer: Does gossip validation correctly reject invalid proposer indices?

reachability.notes: An attacker publishes a sidecar with a proposer_index that is correct according to one client's shuffling but incorrect according to another's. This exploits cross-client proposer assignment divergence.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review gossip validation logic for block and sidecar messages. 2. Verify proposer_index is checked against computed proposer for the slot. 3. Test rejection of messages with incorrect proposer_index values. 4. Verify timing of proposer validation (must occur before further processing). 5. Check for TOCTTOU vulnerabilities where proposer validity could change. 6. Test behavior when receiving messages from future slots within the lookahead window. 7. Attempt to exploit any race conditions in proposer validation during epoch transitions.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0056, Trust Boundary edges tb-010, tb-011. This is the primary trust boundary where external P2P messages are validated. Failure to consistently validate proposer indices across clients enables consensus attacks.
